Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-21 15:00 PDT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood CSM), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood TAM), Lena, Raj, Maya, Tom (Hawthorn)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy): Discussed runtime layout. cost vs latency, dedicated pools, VPC peering steps. Action items captured.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood CSM): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're aiming to run through the runtime intake and make sure we have enough to kick off the lab next week. quick intros?
[00:12] Lena (Hawthorn): Hi, I'm Lena, Head of MLOps at Hawthorn. we're the team that will own deployment.
[00:16] Raj (Hawthorn): Raj here, platform eng. I'll handle the VPC/network bits and infra demos.
[00:22] Maya (Hawthorn): Maya, security. I'll be asking the hard questions.
[00:26] Tom (Hawthorn): Tom, product. I'm curious about cost and SLA tradeoffs.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya — I'll cover runtime config, batching, KV cache, and quantization recs.
[00:34] Marco (Redwood TAM): Marco — I'll walk through the SOC2/KMS integration checklist after the tech piece.

[01:02] Jordan: Great, so high level Hawthorn wants to run a mix of synchronous chat completions and async embeddings for search, is that right? short latencies for chat, and embeddings are bulk.
[01:18] Lena: Correct. majority chat is 60% of requests, avg token length 40 but we do have longer sequences for batch jobs up to 2k tokens occasionally.
[01:30] Priya: OK good, that matters a lot. So we need to balance batching to save token cost for embeddings and long seqs while keeping chat p95 under 150ms ideally, is that the SLO?
[01:42] Tom: p95 150ms would be ideal, if not p99 under 400ms. We can tolerate occasional spikes.
[01:50] Raj: Also FYI, we have very strict egress rules; everything must go over VPC peering and logs go to our KMS-encrypted S3.

[02:20] Priya: Right — so there are two obvious modes: Hosted with VPC connectors or Redwood Dedicated with a private pool inside your VPC (or peered). Hosted is faster to start, but Dedicated gives better predictable throughput and isolation.
[02:36] Lena: We are leaning Dedicated for production. compliance reasons and data residency. But we might test Hosted first.
[02:44] Marco: If Dedicated, we can size a small reserved pool for the pilot. that gives stable tail latency and predictable concurrency.

[03:10] Priya: On batching: for chat workloads, continuous batching helps but you don't want large batch windows. We recommend an adaptive policy: 10–30ms window for chat, larger for embeddings. Also prefix/KV cache for repeated context — that will cut compute for reruns.
[03:32] Lena: Can you explain KV cache behavior again? sometimes those docs are a little dense.
[03:38] Priya: Sure — KV cache stores the past key/value tensors. In practice you'll see big wins if a lot of requests share prefixes (like same system prompt or user history). For hawthorn, if you have many short chats with similar prefaces, prefix cache reduces re-run cost. But caching has memory overhead.
[03:55] Raj: Memory overhead — what's the ballpark on GPU mem when enabling prefix cache for, say, 10k active sessions?
[04:02] Priya: ballpark: depends on sequence length and model size. For 7B quantized model you're looking at X; for 70B it's multiple GBs per session if you cache full KV; we usually recommend selective caching and TTLs. we'll share a calculator.

[04:40] Maya: Security — does cache persist off-GPU and is it encrypted at rest? we need to ensure no sensitive PII remains in plain text.
[04:50] Marco: KV cache lives in memory on the serving nodes; for Dedicated we can configure disk-backed encrypted caches and tie into your KMS. Our default retention is ephemeral but we'll provide settings to scrub or TTL.

[05:20] Tom: On quantization — you mentioned lower-cost variants. How big is the accuracy drop, say 8-bit or 4-bit? we can't degrade UX.
[05:30] Priya: There is model-dependent variance. for many open models, going to 8-bit often preserves quality; 4-bit may have edge cases. Redwood Optimize gives a recommendation by workload and can run evals on your prompt set to measure delta. we'll run a quick eval in the lab.

[06:05] Jordan: Let's talk about cold-starts and scaling behavior. Hawthorn cares about 99th pct tail for chat especially after idle periods.
[06:20] Priya: Cold-start depends on model size and warmup strategies. For Dedicated we can keep a minimal pool in steady-state to absorb spikes, or use a higher baseline for p99s. Also checkpointed weights and faster kernels reduce cold starts.
[06:38] Raj: For VPC peering, what ports and egress do you need? we have a restricted environment.
[06:44] Marco: We'll provide a concise list: subnet CIDRs, allowed ports (TLS 443 + optional monitoring ports), and certificate fingerprints. We'll also support private link if required.

[07:05] Lena: We're concerned about audit logs and traceability. Does Redwood expose per-token tracing or only per-request metrics?
[07:14] Marco: We emit per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns in the console, and you can ship logs to your SIEM with PII redaction rules. We can also increase retention for enterprise plans.

[07:45] Priya: Quick note on routing: you can route by latency vs cost. for non-sensitive embeddings we can route to cheaper quantized variants. For chat pinned to higher QoS, route to a bigger model or Dedicated lane.
[08:02] Tom: Pricing question — does Dedicated still have per-token egress or flat? how do we forecast?
[08:10] Jordan: Dedicated is a committed pool with monthly reservation; there are unit economics docs we'll share. pricing combos: base capacity + overage at known rates. we'll share a forecast template for your traffic.

[08:45] Maya: Regarding encryption, we need HSM-backed key management and FIPS modules. Is that supported?
[08:52] Marco: We integrate with customer KMS and HSM where the cloud supports it; for on-prem we can do HSM attachments. We'll include a matrix of cloud provider support in the pack.

[09:20] Priya: For the lab validation we'll propose two experiments: 1) steady-state throughput for embeddings at target qps and 2) chat p95/p99 under burst patterns including cold starts. We need your sample traffic and a representative prompt set.
[09:35] Lena: We'll pull a two-week slice of logs and also create a focused 1000-record prompt set for evals.

[10:00] Raj: Network wise, we can spin up VPC peering in the test account; what's the minimum Terraform we need?
[10:05] Marco: We'll share a reference Terraform module for peerings and the security group snippets. small glue script, nothing fancy.

[10:40] Priya: A note on failover: you can configure automatic fallback to hosted variants in another region if Dedicated capacity is saturated — tradeoff is data crossing. for regulated data you might block fallback.
[10:57] Lena: For us, fallback only if it's within our VPC and under our control; cross-border fallback is not acceptable.

[11:20] Tom: Another product question — can we do canary rollouts by model version? we want to test a quantized variant against the standard one.
[11:29] Priya: Yes, rollouts supported: percentage splits, canary windows, and automatic rollback on regressions. we can tie eval metrics to the rollback triggers.

[12:02] Jordan: Ok let's pin concrete dates: Marco to send SOC2 + KMS checklist by tomorrow 7/22; Priya to share runtime and batching template by Friday 7/23; Lena to share logs by 7/26; lab week target 7/27. sound good?
[12:18] All: yes/ack.

[12:40] Maya: Quick clarification — will Redwood store the raw logs during the lab? we prefer ephemeral handling.
[12:48] Marco: We will not persist raw PII logs in our systems for the pilot unless you opt in; by default we stream to your S3 and run ephemeral evals.

[13:10] Raj: If we discover a need for a larger baseline pool after the lab, what's the commit cadence? monthly, quarterly?
[13:18] Jordan: We have flexible reserved tiers; pilot can convert to monthly or annual reserved pool. We'll provide the commercial options in the follow-up.

[13:45] Priya: Any unknown blockers from your side?
[13:50] Lena: main blocker is getting the traffic slice scrubbed quickly — security will need to sign off.
[13:56] Maya: I'll own scrub and ensure PII is removed before sharing.

[14:20] Jordan: Great. we'll recap next steps in email and attach the artifacts. Thanks all, meeting ended.

--- End Transcript ---
